question.worked_solution:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}(\theta )\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

When $r(\theta )=2\theta $, ${\theta }_{1}=0$ and ${\theta }_{2}=\frac{\pi }{2}$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(2\theta )^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}4{\theta }^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\theta }^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2(\frac{{\theta }^{3}}{3}){|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =2(\frac{(\pi /2)^{3}}{3})-2(\frac{{0}^{3}}{3}) \\  & =\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$
